# S403 — ork wait: several runs, every run of a project, and stage ends

`ork wait RUN...` and `ork wait --project P` block until one of the named runs, or one of P's unfinished runs, changes state, then print one line per run that changed in that read and exit with a code that tells which change it was. `--stage` also ends the wait when a role round of a followed run ends. The daemon sends a notice when a run record's state, pending question or ended role count changes, so the wait wakes at once instead of on its 30 s read.

**Findings:** 2026-11-17: the relay orchestrator follows two or three runs at once (relay concurrency 2 cloud + 1 local) and polled them with shell loops around `ork status`, because `ork wait` (S257) follows one run only: it takes at most one RUN (`internal/cli/wait.go:45-47`), and `--project P` with more than one unfinished run is a usage error (`internal/cli/wait.go:270-273`, adj 203 `cli.wait-default-run`). It also wakes only on a `snapshot.changed` notice or every 30 s (`internal/cli/wait.go:29-34`), since a run record change sends no notice (`internal/daemon/runs.go:233` feeds only the S311 notifier). · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

## Why

Owner rule (2026-11-17): a deterministic step done regularly is code, not a hand loop or a model call. This session the orchestrator ran `while ...; do ork status ...; sleep ...; done` loops to learn when a run landed, stopped, paused on a question or awaited approval, because:

- `ork wait` takes one RUN (`internal/cli/wait.go:45-47`) and `--project` refuses a project with several unfinished runs (`internal/cli/wait.go:234-274`; adj 203, decision a: "an error if there are several").
- A record change sends no subscriber notice: `deps.Store.OnChange` goes only to the S311 notifier (`internal/daemon/runs.go:233`, `internal/daemon/notify.go:51`), and `snapshot.changed` is sent for cached parts (`internal/daemon/subscribe.go:78-89`) and after a landing (`internal/daemon/landed.go:240`). So `ork wait` falls back to a read every 30 s (`internal/cli/wait.go:29`).
- There is no way to wait for "the implementer round ended" short of polling `ork show`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-17): `--project P` follows every unfinished run of P at the start [cli.wait-project, adj 449, supersedes adj 203]. Exit codes stay 0/3/4/5 with 3 (question) over 0 (state change), plus 6 when every printed line is a stage end [cli.wait-exit-codes, adj 450, supersedes adj 201]. The wait learns of a record change from `snapshot.changed` for part `runs` with an optional run list [cli.wait-signal, adj 451].

## Implement

1. Red tests above.
2. Daemon: wrap `deps.Store.OnChange` so it calls the S311 notifier and then `d.changed(project, source.Runs)` with the run ID, but only when the state, the pending kind or key, or the number of role rounds with `ended_at` set differs between before and after. Add `Runs []string` with `json:"runs,omitempty"` to `SnapshotChanged` (additive; older clients ignore it).
3. CLI: `waiter` holds a list of runs with a base state each. Positional RUN... (one or more); `--project P` resolves to every unfinished run of P at the start (runs started later are not followed). One read per followed run on each wake; a run that is final and matches nothing is dropped with the stderr line above; when none are left, exit 4.
4. A wait ends on the first read in which at least one followed run is done by `judge`. Print one line per done run in the order given: `RUN ITEM STATE`, then ` key: KEY` for a question, then ` next: CMD` when there is one. One RUN keeps today's multi-line text and JSON. With more than one run, `--json` prints an array of the existing `waitJSON` objects.
5. `--stage`: a followed run whose ended role round count grew since the last read is done with `RUN ITEM stage ROLE round N ended EXIT`. Exit code precedence over all printed lines: 3 (question) > 0 (state change) > 6 (stage end only).
6. Docs: `docs/guide.md` Wait for a change and the usage text; `docs/design.md` (the notice). CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.
7. UI slice: UI pass (r14), since `internal/cli` output changes.

Owner decisions (2026-11-18): What JSON does ork wait --json print for a stage end? -> waitJSON stage: one object, or one array element when several runs are followed, with state "stage" and reason "ROLE round N ended EXIT" [cli.wait-stage-json].

## Check

Acceptance criteria:
- 'ork wait r1 r2 --until landed,stopped,question,awaiting-approval' returns as soon as either run reaches one of those states, prints one line per changed run, and exits 3 when a question is among them, else 0.
- 'ork wait --project P' follows every unfinished run of P instead of refusing.
- 'ork wait RUN --stage' returns with exit 6 when a role round ends.
- A state change reaches a waiting 'ork wait' without the 30 s poll.
- 'ork wait RUN' with one run prints what it printed before.
